summary: Client-side final chunk suppressed when SSE 'event-id' header duplicated after transparent proxy redirect
description:
Issue summary: BrightTutor reports that students intermittently receive truncated final paragraphs from assistant responses when the app experiences an HTTP redirect shortly before an SSE reconnect. Impact: customer-visible partial outputs in production for a subset of sessions; impacts student experience during interactive tutoring flows. Scope: ~2% of streaming sessions over the last 48h from us-east region for this customer; not all reconnects are affected.

Observed behavior: After a transparent redirect at the edge (302 from the CDN to a regional gateway), the client reconnects and receives streaming fragments but never sees the closing 'data: [DONE]' style event for some sessions; final tokens are missing. Server-side logs show the final fragment was emitted and acknowledged by the downstream LB, but the client SDK reports it dropped due to duplicate event identifiers.

Expected behavior: Reconnect should resume or re-stream the missing tail such that the client receives the complete finalization event and the last tokens.

Why this matters: Dedicated customers rely on predictable streaming completion for user-facing flows (final paragraph, JSON termination). Partial outputs are causing user confusion and support escalations.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use BrightTutor app with SSE-based assistant session against prod us-east endpoint.
2) Trigger a server-side redirect by simulating CDN regional redirection (internal test harness provided to customer).
3) Allow the client library to reconnect automatically (SDK default reconnect settings).
4) Observe that in some reconnects the final 'end' event does not reach the client even though server shows emission in logs.
logs: Server-side trace (serving-runtime): emitted final chunk id=evt-9f4b2c at 2026-03-10T18:12:23.456Z, status=sent to lb-az3, ack=200

LB (regional-gateway) extract: received request via CDN redirect; preserved header X-Stream-ID: stream-78e9; original event-id: evt-9f4b2c; forwarded to backend with event-id header duplicated by proxy rewrite
Client SDK console: SSE fragment received (event-id: evt-9f4b2c) but dropped because already-seen event-id in local dedupe cache; last visible token ends in '...students can' (incomplete sentence)
investigation_notes: Support verified request/response timeline with BrightTutor's request IDs; timestamps align between emitting server and LB acknowledgements.
Captured a small set of live traces where the LB performed a redirect then proxied the new connection but duplicated the original 'event-id' header on the reissued stream initiation.

Client SDK (v1.4.2) contains a deduplication step keyed on 'event-id' to guard against replay; when the same event-id appears after reconnect the SDK treats the fragment as a duplicate and discards it, which suppresses the finalization event in cases where the client state had been partially advanced.

Hypothesis: LB redirect + proxy rewrite path duplicates event-id in the handoff window, producing a false-positive duplicate detection on client side and dropping terminal fragment. Not an issue when LB rewrites to fresh event-id or when reconnect completes without redirect.
We reproduced locally by running a dev proxy that injects original event-id into proxied reconnect; reproduces client-side suppression ~90% of the time with current SDK dedupe window settings.
workaround: Customer guidance sent: temporary mitigation is to upgrade client to SDK v1.4.4 (hotfix) which ignores dedupe for tags with 'final' meta (patch attached) OR configure CDN to not preserve incoming 'event-id' header on redirect. Both options reduce occurrence while server-side fix is planned.
next_actions: 1) Engineering (serving-runtime) to add defensiveness: append a stream-instance UUID to emitted event-ids on the backend so event-ids are globally unique across reconnects (PR planned).
2) Edge/Platform to change redirect behavior to strip preserved 'event-id' on transparent redirects (config change scheduled for 2026-03-14 canary).

3) Client SDK team to release formal SDK patch (v1.4.4) that treats an event-id collision during a reconnect as a potential resume marker and requests missing tail if detected (patch merged, release candidate available).
4) Communicate to BrightTutor with ETA for the platform fix and offer a targeted canary for their traffic once ready.
